rationale: A wins because it knows where the floorboards are weak and labels them before a reporter falls through. Its line, "Without a named customer this is a roadmap story," is exactly the discipline this assignment needed. B has good instincts, but "220 million users already inside companies" and "the legal team can make a slide deck without asking design" are decorations on facts the update did not give. That is how a decent angle turns into a cleanup job.
gaps_in_A: "220 million free users" is not supported. The update says 220 million monthly users, not that they are free users.

"Canva walks its 220 million users into Adobe and Microsoft's enterprise turf" slightly overconverts a consumer-scale user count into enterprise leverage; it still needs evidence of workplace usage or enterprise demand.
"growing into the valuation" is a smart finance question, but the angle stays thin without valuation timing, revenue, or enterprise pipeline numbers.
gaps_in_B: "220 million users already inside companies" is invented. The update gives monthly users, not workplace penetration.

"Notion, Figma, and Miro ran the same arc. Canva is the largest consumer-originated design tool to attempt it." This may be plausible context, but it is not in the update and needs proof before it belongs in the angle.
"the legal team can make a slide deck without asking design" invents a user, workflow, and output format. No legal team, slide deck, or non-designer use case is supplied.

"Enterprise contracts introduce stickier, higher-ASP revenue and reduce churn risk" asserts the economics before pricing, contract size, customer mix, or retention data exist. That is analyst cosplay until proven.
